description: A customizable AI chat with multiple providers (OpenAI/ChatGPT, Anthropic/Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, Cloudflare Workers AI, Kimi, Qwen, and free NVIDIA models).
viewsContainers.chat.title: OpenVS Thor
views.chat.name: OpenVS Thor
config.skills: Custom skills (named instruction packs) as `{ id, name, description, instructions }`. They appear in the skill picker and `/skill <id>`, and override built-ins with the same id. Skills can also live in `.openvs/skills/<id>.md`.
config.mcp.servers: Global MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, as a map of `id` → `{ command, args, env, cwd }`. Their tools become available to the agent (namespaced `mcp__<id>__<tool>`). Projects can add servers via `.openvs/mcp.json` or `.vscode/mcp.json`. stdio servers only start in a trusted workspace.
config.defaultProvider: The AI provider selected by default when the chat opens.
config.openai.model: Default model for the OpenAI provider.
config.openai.baseUrl: Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible API. Change this to use a proxy or compatible endpoint.
config.anthropic.model: Default model for the Anthropic provider.
config.anthropic.baseUrl: Base URL for the Anthropic API.
config.nvidia.model: Default model for the NVIDIA provider. NVIDIA offers a generous free tier via build.nvidia.com.
config.nvidia.baseUrl: Base URL for the NVIDIA OpenAI-compatible API.
config.gemini.model: Default model for the Google Gemini provider. Get a free API key at aistudio.google.com.
config.gemini.baseUrl: Base URL for Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API.
config.provider.antigravity: Google Antigravity (sign in with your Google account — ToS restricts this credential to Google's own client; prefer Google Gemini above with an AI Studio key unless you specifically need Antigravity's model set)
config.antigravity.model: Default model for the Google Antigravity provider.
config.provider.openrouter: OpenRouter (one key, hundreds of models incl. free ones)
config.provider.groq: Groq (free tier — no credit card, rate-limited)
config.groq.model: Default model for the Groq provider. Groq's free tier needs no credit card; it is limited by requests and tokens per minute, applied per organization.
config.groq.baseUrl: Base URL for Groq's OpenAI-compatible API.
config.provider.mistral: Mistral (free 'Experiment' tier — requires opting in to data training)
config.mistral.model: Default model for the Mistral provider. The free Experiment tier reaches every model but requires opting in to having your data used for training; exact rate limits are shown in the Mistral Admin Console under Limits.
config.mistral.baseUrl: Base URL for the Mistral La Plateforme API.
config.provider.cloudflare: Cloudflare Workers AI (free daily allocation — needs an account ID as well as a token)
config.cloudflare.accountId: Your Cloudflare account ID. Required: Workers AI puts it in the request URL, so an API token on its own is not enough. Find it on the Workers & Pages overview page in the Cloudflare dashboard.
config.cloudflare.model: Default model for the Cloudflare Workers AI provider, e.g. @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast. The free allocation is 10,000 Neurons per day and renews daily.
config.cloudflare.baseUrl: Base URL for Cloudflare Workers AI's OpenAI-compatible API. {account_id} is replaced with the account ID setting above.
config.openrouter.model: Default model for the OpenRouter provider. Models with a ':free' suffix cost nothing.
config.openrouter.baseUrl: Base URL for the OpenRouter API.
config.kimi.model: Default model for the Kimi (Moonshot AI) provider.
config.kimi.baseUrl: Base URL for the Moonshot AI API. Use https://api.moonshot.cn/v1 for China-mainland accounts.
config.qwen.model: Default model for the Qwen (DashScope) provider.
config.qwen.baseUrl: Base URL for DashScope's OpenAI-compatible mode. Use https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 for Beijing-region accounts.
config.custom.model: Default model for the custom provider (e.g. an Ollama model tag).
config.custom.baseUrl: Base URL of any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Defaults to a local Ollama install; point it at LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, or any other compatible server.
config.authUrl: Optional web sign-in URL for this provider. When set, a 'Sign in with web' button is shown; the editor opens this URL with redirect_uri & state query params and stores the token returned to its URI callback. Point this at your own OAuth/proxy service to let users log in instead of pasting a key.
config.agent.maxSteps: Maximum number of tool-use steps the agent may take before pausing. Resuming after a token-limit cutoff does not count against this budget. Under the Full Auto approval policy a run extends itself past this budget rather than pausing, up to a hard ceiling of 2× — every stricter policy stops here and waits for "continue".
config.agent.maxContextTokens: Approximate token budget for the conversation sent to the model. 0 (default) sizes it automatically from the model's known context window. Set a positive number to pin it. Once exceeded, older turns are compacted/trimmed so long sessions don't fail with a context-length error.
config.ask.autoContext: What Ask mode automatically attaches when you haven't attached anything: just the active file (default), every open editor tab, or nothing. Tool-capable models can read further files themselves either way.
config.stream.idleTimeoutMs: Abort a streaming reply if the provider sends no data for this many milliseconds. Prevents a dropped connection from leaving the chat waiting forever.
config.agent.commandTimeoutMs: Maximum time (ms) a shell command run by the agent may take before it is killed. Must comfortably exceed a full build or test run, or verification steps get cut off midway.
config.agent.shell: Shell used to run the agent's commands (e.g. "C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\bash.exe" or "/bin/zsh"). Leave empty to detect one: /bin/sh elsewhere, and on Windows the Git Bash that ships with Git, falling back to PowerShell and then cmd.exe. Models write POSIX shell by default, so Git Bash is preferred where it exists.
config.agent.maxSubagents: Maximum number of sub-agents a single run may spawn (cost/safety cap).
config.agent.maxSubagentDepth: How deeply sub-agents may nest (a sub-agent spawning sub-agents). 1 disables nesting.
config.agent.parallelResearch: Run read-only research sub-agents in parallel. Write-capable sub-agents always run sequentially.
config.agent.parallelReads: Run a step's adjacent read-only tool calls (read_file, list_dir, glob_files, search_files) concurrently instead of one after another. They take no approval and change nothing, so serializing them only added latency. Turn off on a workspace where concurrent file access is a problem.
config.agent.maxRunMinutes: Wall-clock ceiling for a single agent run, in minutes. The step budget limits how many times the model is asked, not how long each ask takes — on a queued free tier one step can stall for many minutes without the step count moving. 0 disables the ceiling. Reaching it ends the run with an explanation; "continue" resumes.
config.agent.traceTiming: Report each agent step's duration and prompt size in the chat. Off by default. Turn it on to tell a run that is slow because the conversation has grown large from one that is slow because the provider is queueing requests.
config.remote.traceSessions: Log where the host's own shadow copy of session state (built only from traffic it already sees) diverges from what the chat panel actually sent, to a dedicated "OpenVS Chat: Sessions (Shadow)" output channel. Off by default. Diagnostic only: the shadow copy is compared, never acted on, and the chat panel stays authoritative either way.
config.remote.loopback: Register a hidden message sink that writes every message the chat host broadcasts as one JSON line per message to a dedicated "OpenVS Chat: Loopback Sink" output channel — no network involved. Exists to exercise the multi-sink code paths (origin-aware routing, prompt rebind, escalation) without a real remote client connected. Off by default; a reload picks up a change.
config.remote.promptEscalationSeconds: How long an approval or question prompt waits for a chat-capable surface (the sidebar chat panel, or a paired remote device in a later release) to answer before falling back to a native VS Code dialog. Only matters once every chat-capable surface has disconnected while a prompt is pending.
config.remote.enabled: Turn on remote control: dials out to the relay configured in "openvsChat.remote.relayUrl" so a paired phone can drive this chat panel. Off by default. Requires an open folder or workspace (to derive a room) and a relay URL — see the "OpenVS Thor: Remote: Deploy Your Own Relay" command to deploy one, or "OpenVS Thor: Remote: Enable Remote Control" once you have one.
config.remote.relayUrl: The base URL of your own deployed OpenVS relay (a Cloudflare Worker — see openvs-relay/, `wrangler deploy`). Empty by default: there is no default relay, since shipping one would mean operating infrastructure for every user. Remote control stays off until this is set.
config.remote.deviceTokenDays: How many days a paired device's token stays valid before the host revokes it (a sliding window, refreshed on use). Enforced by an hourly host-side sweep against each device's creation time — the relay itself has no notion of this setting.
config.remote.idleDisableHours: Auto-disconnect remote control after this many hours with no activity from the desktop host, as a safety net against a forgotten open connection. The live connection is disconnected, not the "openvsChat.remote.enabled" setting itself; the next activity from the desktop host resumes it.
config.remote.approvalFloor: The strictest "openvsChat.guardrails.approval" a remotely-initiated run is allowed to relax below (default 'auto-edits'). A run started from the desktop webview always uses your own guardrails.approval setting unchanged, including 'yolo' — but a run started from a paired phone needs an interlock the desktop user can see and veto, since a stolen device token would otherwise be a silent remote shell with nothing to push-notify about. 'auto-edits' rather than 'always' because what actually matters is the shell: 'run_command' is what a remote client should not run unattended, while workspace edits are recoverable and a card per file edit would make the phone unusable. Approval cards raised by a remote run still fan out to every connected surface, so the desktop can always veto.
config.rules: Always-on instructions ('rules') prepended to every conversation, in addition to the system prompt. Use this to enforce conventions and constraints.
config.ruleFiles: Workspace files to load as rules when present (first lines win on truncation). Lets you keep project rules in the repo, e.g. AGENTS.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md.
config.guardrails.approval: When the agent must ask before side effects. 'always' prompts for every write and command; 'auto-edits' auto-approves file edits inside the workspace but still prompts for commands; 'yolo' auto-approves writes and commands (default). The hard guardrails always apply: blocked commands, protected paths, the workspace root, and untrusted workspaces are enforced whatever this is set to. Reading, listing and searching never prompt.
config.guardrails.approval.always: Prompt before every file write and command (safest).
config.guardrails.approval.autoEdits: Auto-approve file edits inside the workspace; still prompt before running commands.
config.guardrails.approval.yolo: Auto-approve writes and commands without prompting; only the hard guardrails apply (default).
config.guardrails.deniedCommands: Regular expressions (case-insensitive). A command matching any of these is blocked outright, before approval.
config.guardrails.allowedCommands: If non-empty, the agent may ONLY run commands matching one of these regular expressions (an allow-list).
config.guardrails.protectedPaths: Glob-like patterns the agent may never write to (e.g. .git, .env, key files).
config.auto.decompose: In Auto + Agent mode, split the plan into steps and run a sub-agent per step (planner decomposition) instead of a single implementer.
config.auto.planModel: Model used for the **planning** phase when the provider is set to **Auto**. Format: `provider:model` (e.g. `anthropic:claude-opus-4-0`). Leave empty to let OpenVS pick the best available model based on which keys are configured.
config.auto.codeModel: Model used for the **implementation** phase in **Auto** mode. Format: `provider:model` (e.g. `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-0`). Must be a tool-capable model. Leave empty to auto-select.
config.auto.reviewModel: Model used for the **review** phase in **Auto** mode. Format: `provider:model` (e.g. `openai:gpt-4o`). Leave empty to auto-select.
config.auto.enableReview: When using Auto mode in Agent, run a final review pass over the agent's changes with the review model.
config.persona.thinking: Ask the model to reason inside a <thinking> block before answering (shown inline as "🤔 Thinking…"). Turn off for models that reason natively or to tighten output.
config.persona.environment: Include a workspace environment snapshot (git branch and status, platform, open files) in the system prompt so answers are grounded in your project state.
config.systemPrompt: System prompt prepended to every conversation.
config.maxTokens: Maximum number of tokens to generate per response round. When a response hits this limit, the chat automatically continues it in place (up to 8 rounds), so long answers and big code blocks are not cut off midway. Non-inline Edit mode (which asks for a whole file back) always uses at least 8192 regardless of this setting.
